grant: Diocesan Grant Application (plus BCIM and CNAMB school/religious-education grants)
eligibility: The Black and Indian Mission Office Diocesan Grant application is open to all Dioceses with African American and Native American/Alaska Native communities, funding evangelization outreach and ministry programs, religious education programs in parishes and Catholic schools, and faith formation programs for African American and Native American children and adults.

Organizations must reflect Mrs. Doheny's Mission & Mandate and fall within one of four funding areas: Social Welfare, Health and Wellness, Education, or Religion. Only grant seekers currently registered and in good standing as 501(c)(3) with the IRS and the Attorney General of California's Registry of Charities will be considered. 'Funding is generally limited to Los Angeles County. In some instances, Los Angeles programs of organizations headquartered elsewhere may be funded.' Organizations may apply once a year; the Board does not meet in July, September, or November; review can take up to three months.

grant: Endowment and Donor Advised Fund Distributions
eligibility: The Catholic Community Foundation of the Archdiocese of Baltimore 'enables individuals, families and organizations to establish Endowments and Donor Advised Funds to help perpetuate the work of parishes, schools, outreach programs, and other Catholic ministries.' Grants flow from donor-established funds: 'Since inception, over $50 million has been distributed to Archdiocesan schools, parishes, and ministries' and 'Over $5.3 million dollars in grant distributions in 2025.' No competitive application cycle is published on the site.

Tabor Fund awards 'provide an opportunity for applicants to refresh and/or re-energize their spirituality, faith, mind and/or physical wellbeing, as part of fostering personal development and improving their ministry,' in the categories Education and Formation, and Sabbaticals and Retreats. Eligibility: 'Any bona fide employee (paid or volunteer), lay, deacons or religious who works in a recognized ministry and is actively serving the Catholic Diocese of Cleveland. Attendant parishes, schools or organizations that are engaged in a recognized ministry are eligible to apply.' Grant funds must go to the sponsoring organization (parish or school), not to the individual. Amount: Up to $1,500. The foundation's Catholic Community Fund line reads: 'No unsolicited grants accepted at this time.'

grant: Education, Lay Leadership and Community Grant Cycle
eligibility: Organizations seeking grants should align with one of four focus areas: Education (Catholic schools and religious education K-12); Leadership Development ('Forming leaders for parishes, schools and agencies who can engage others in creating a vision, strategies and infrastructures to advance the Church'); Community Building ('initiatives that strengthen families and parishes'); or Health Care in Milwaukee (St. Anthony Fund). 'We focus on organizations listed in the Official Catholic Directory. Other tax-exempt 501(c)(3) organizations whose missions are consistent with that of the church may also apply.' 'The majority of a fund's grants should be directed to the 10 counties of the Archdiocese of Milwaukee.' Two-step process: Letter of Intent, then full proposal by invitation.

grant: Formation and Action Grants Program (with Small Group and Parish Ministry grants)
eligibility: Formation and Action Grants fund the formation of priests, parish staff, and parishioners in Catholic social teaching and its application in parish life; grants range from $250 to $4,000 and applications are accepted mid-August to late September each year. Small Group Grants: 'Any parish in the Archdiocese of Saint Paul and Minneapolis is welcome to apply' ($250–$2,000). Preschool, Youth, and Young Adult Ministry Grants: 'Projects must benefit people in parishes in the Archdiocese of St. Paul and Minneapolis' ($250–$3,000). There is also a professional development grant line for lay ecclesial ministers.

'Who may apply: Nonprofits listed in the current Clarion Herald Catholic directory serving the eight civil parishes of the Archdiocese of New Orleans.' 'Schools and parishes within the geographic footprint of the Archdiocese will be considered in a future funding year and are not eligible for 2027 grant funding.' Every proposal must align with the 2027 impact area: 'Youth, Young Adults, and the Family (Faith Formation and Human Formation).' Grants in three categories: Up to $10,000; $10,001 to $25,000; $25,001 to $35,000 — apply in only one category; organizations awarded in 2026 may not apply in 2027. Applications accepted October 1 to November 30, 2026.

grant: Parish Endowments Matching Program (1:1 match, up to $5,000)
grantor: Catholic Community Foundation (Archdiocese of San Antonio)
eligibility: The Catholic Community Foundation serves parishes, schools, and Catholic ministries across South Central Texas and throughout the 19 counties of the Archdiocese of San Antonio. An endowment with Catholic Community Foundation is a permanently restricted fund created to provide long-term financial sustainability for a designated Catholic organization or ministry. Per the Archdiocese of San Antonio grants landscape: PARISH ENDOWMENTS MATCHING PROGRAM - First Endowment for Parish Community - 1:1 Match - Up to $5,000.

grant: National Scholarships and Contests; National Projects & Charities
eligibility: The 2027 Scholarship and Contest Forms Are Available in the National Quarterly... separate Scholarship and Contest sections in the Members area. Donate to a Specific National Project or Charity (National Projects and Charities Donation Form).

grantor: Catholic Education Foundation of the Diocese of Joliet
eligibility: The Catholic Education Foundation scholarship program enables students and their families to obtain the promise of a Catholic education. The program is open to K-12 students with demonstrated financial need currently enrolled or applying for the next school year in any CEF-supported Catholic schools within the Diocese of Joliet. The standard CEF scholarship is $1,000 per student. A family must apply each year through FACTS Grant and Aid Assessment to qualify for a scholarship. All awards are made based on financial need.

'Catholic Extension Society can only consider funding requests that are submitted by our pre-designated Extension Dioceses, and requested as a part of the overall strategic plan and funding priorities for the year from Catholic Extension Society to the diocese. Catholic Extension Society cannot consider funding applications from any other organizations, entities, or individuals.' All funding requests must be submitted in coordination with the diocese's designated primary contact with Catholic Extension Society. Funding categories: Building Foundation; Building Leaders ('Funds the education/training of lay and ordained leaders'); Building Churches and other Facilities; Engaging Young Catholics ('Supports ministries that provide faith formation for children, teens, and young adults and families'); Building Capacity; Enhancing Pastoral and Social Ministry.

contact_name: Lisa Oliveras, Legacy Gifts and Grants Coordinator
eligibility: Grants will be awarded to Catholic compliant non-profit organizations whose serve the spiritual or corporal needs of the people of Central Florida. Applications must demonstrate that grant will be used for a specific program which will directly serve people within the nine counties (Orange, Osceola, Seminole, Marion, Lake, Volusia, Brevard, Polk and Sumter) of the Diocese of Orlando. We have two versions of our online grant application: Diocesan Parishes, Schools and Ministries -or- Non-Diocesan Nonprofits. Application Deadline: June 1, 2026 at 5:00PM.

contact_name: Ann Letteer, CFRE — Director of Programs
eligibility: Each spring and fall, The Catholic Foundation awards Dallas-area Catholic schools, churches and non-profit 501(c)3 organizations grants through the unrestricted Philanthropy Fund as well as endowment funds which support specific purposes. Eligibility per the Grant Guidelines PDF: Catholic Organizations in the Diocese of Dallas; Organizations not recognized by the Diocese of Dallas but serving an identifiable Catholic population must include written support from an active member of clergy in the Dallas Diocese; Grant requests up to $100,000 will be considered.

grant: 2026-2027 Grant Programs (incl. Evangelization and Worship; Women in Philanthropy)
eligibility: Applicants should confirm that they meet all eligibility requirements before applying: The organization or project is Catholic in identity, sponsored by a Catholic entity, or clearly aligned with Catholic mission and values. The organization is recognized as a tax-exempt nonprofit under section 501(c)(3). The proposed work benefits the Delaware Valley community. Appropriate institutional approval is available, such as a pastor, principal, or executive director.

grant: Advancing the Mission Evangelization & Lifelong Catechesis Grants
grantor: Catholic Foundation for the Diocese of Green Bay
eligibility: The Catholic Foundation offers grants to financially support the spiritual, educational, and social needs of communities across Northeastern Wisconsin. This includes Catholic parishes and schools, Catholic entities, and other 501 c(3) charitable organizations that align with Catholic teachings within the Catholic Diocese of Green Bay. Most grant applications are accepted from October 1 to December 1.

grant: Impact Grants (incl. Empowering Catholic Education & Formation)
eligibility: Nonprofit entities in Michigan that serve communities primarily in Michigan. The organization's mission, values and behaviors are in line with Catholic Teachings. Organization is a U.S. 501(c)(3) with audited financial statements. Project addresses one or more of the funding focus areas: social outreach, education/formation, and parish life.

The Grants Program directly impacts nonprofits, parishes, and schools serving the general community within the boundaries of the Archdiocese of Atlanta. Our grants support nonprofit organizations which are tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3) of the IRS code, and whose mission, values and behaviors are not in conflict with Catholic teachings. Catholic Community Grants - August 1-31: Applications open for parishes, nonprofits, and Catholic ministries. Grant awards vary ranging from $2,000 - $10,000 ... Funding for projects in alignment with Catholic Social Teachings and Works of Mercy are provided by endowment funds that support organizations' work honoring the sanctity of life, serving the disabled, caring for the elderly, serving the homeless, and other community service programs such as health and mental health programs.

For the 2026 Grant Program, there will be grants available to parishes, schools, ministries, and other Catholic entities within the Archdiocese of Kansas City in Kansas. Grants will be made available for purposes that align with the Catholic Foundation's mission to collaborate with parishes, schools, ministries, and institutions to facilitate Catholic giving. The maximum grant will be $5,000 and will be for no more than 50% of the project cost. The grant application will open on July 1, 2026, and applications will be received through 4:00 pm on August 31, 2026.

grant: Endowment Fund Disbursements (no competitive grant program)
eligibility: The Catholic Foundation practices Christian stewardship by managing individual endowment funds for the benefit of parishes, schools and agencies in the Diocese of Sacramento. Each year, an endowment's earnings are used to help finance the specific purpose for which it was created. The Catholic Foundation is organized as a supporting organization to the Roman Catholic Bishop of Sacramento, a corporation sole, all 102 local parishes of the Diocese of Sacramento, and various Catholic agencies with the Diocese of Sacramento.

grant: Mother Teresa Women's Giving Circle Grants
eligibility: The Mother Teresa Women's Giving Circle funds nonprofits located within the Diocese of Houma-Thibodaux for projects specifically impacting Women, Children and Families. All nonprofits who fit within those categories are invited to submit a Letter of Intent starting December 1st, and the grant committee will review and open of the Grant Process to those approved through the LOI stage.

The CMI Fund has recently set aside an additional $300,000 to be awarded in 2025 for grants ranging in size between $10,000 and $50,000 to up to six (arch)dioceses who are serious about implementing new and/or enhanced marriage ministry programs which are in alignment with the aforementioned Pastoral Framework and the goals and objectives of the CMI Fund.

Local Courts have an opportunity to raise funds and receive Partnership Funding from the High Court for one major cause each year. Program goals: to support significant diocesan, seminary, and Catholic educational appeals. The sponsoring local court will receive dollar-for-dollar Partnership Funding when raising $1,000 to $2,500.

grant: Foundation Grant Programs (Chastity & Abstinence Education, Education Technology, Event Sponsorship, Matching Grants)
grantor: Catholic United Financial, a Trusted Fraternal Life brand
eligibility: Grant programs are limited to individuals and organizations located in the areas where Catholic United Financial is licensed to do business: Minnesota, Iowa, North Dakota, South Dakota and Wisconsin. Grants help parishes, Catholic schools, ministries and other organizations; Chastity and Abstinence Education grants of up to $1,000 go to schools or parishes for programs, events, curriculum or media offering education to youth in collaboration with other parishes, youth groups, schools, regional or diocesan-wide efforts.

grantor: Catholic United Financial, a Trusted Fraternal Life brand
eligibility: Grants4Good is a program that allows Catholic United to provide funds that enhance events in parishes and communities. By offering grant opportunities in the areas of service, family, and faith, we are able to see Catholic communities thrive and grow. Grants up to $500 are available to parishes and schools through a local Parish Volunteer Team or Council.
Eligible Applicants: Non-profit organizations within the United States

Funding priorities: organizations that are 'Catholic and/or faith-oriented,' active in Dutchtown/Gravois Park and North St. Louis communities, assisting immigrants and refugees, expanding safe housing, serving youth and/or women, improving economic mobility, or alleviating food insecurity. Excluded sectors include advocacy/convening organizations, endowments and capital campaigns, and local affiliates or branches of national organizations. Requirements: '- Are situated within the St. Louis region, including the City, County, and East St. Louis. - Are a 501(c)(3) in good standing and/or has a fiscal agent. - Have not received funding from the Incarnate Word Foundation in the past three consecutive years.'

grantor: The John G. & Marie Stella Kenedy Memorial Foundation
eligibility: All grant applications must be considered annually at the Board of Directors meetings in May of each year. To be considered in May, an application must be received by October 15th of the previous year. All grant funds must be used exclusively within Texas and exclusively for religious, educational or charitable purposes. The Foundation makes grants to non-profit organizations that are 501(c)(3) charitable organizations under the Internal Revenue Service Code. To be considered for a grant, an applicant must be listed in the IRS Publication 78 or the Official Catholic Directory, as appropriate. Note to Sectarian applicants: Application procedures differ among Diocese. Please check with your Diocese before applying to ensure that you comply with Diocese protocols.

Many councils create and run their own service projects, depending on the makeup of their members and their community's needs. In addition, the Knights of Columbus recommends the following, official programs in the categories of Faith, Family, Community and Life and supports councils in implementing them.

The Koch Foundation supports Catholic non-profit organizations as recognized by the Catholic hierarchy of Rome. US Applicants: Organizations in the United States are required to meet the following: 1. Identified and recognized by United States Official Catholic Directory (OCD) published by P.J. Kenedy & Sons 2. Possess a letter from the U.S. IRS proving their exemption from federal taxes (specifically 501(c)(3)). Each application must include a letter of support from the diocesan ordinary where the project will take place. Dioceses, eparchies, and religious institutes of pontifical right may submit up to six (6) requests per year.

grant: National Initiative to Strengthen Christian Campus Ministries at Colleges and Universities (Campus Ministry Initiative)
eligibility: Charitable organizations in the United States that support Christian campus ministries at or near multiple colleges and universities in the United States and that are tax-exempt public charities under Internal Revenue Code section 501(c)(3) ... Eligible organizations may include national and regional denominational agencies, campus ministry parachurch organizations, collegiate ministry associations, church networks and independent religious agencies, among others. ... individual local campus ministries, congregations that support students on a single campus, or Christian study centers based at a single university are not eligible to apply.

grant: National Initiative to Strengthen Chaplaincies at Colleges and Universities (Chaplaincy Initiative)
eligibility: In this competitive initiative, the Endowment intends to award grants of up to $2.5 million each to approximately 60 accredited, four-year colleges and universities in the United States with chaplaincies or offices of religious life. ... Interested colleges and universities must submit concept papers ... by January 11, 2027.

Eligible charitable organizations located in the United States were able submit proposals to create new or enhance existing programs that advance one or both of the following objectives: Supporting congregations (especially pastors, children and youth ministry staff and congregational volunteer leaders) and other Christian organizations by developing and providing resources, programs and educational opportunities ... to help interested parents and caregivers share their Christian faith and values with their children(round now closed).

Charitable organizations in the United States that are tax-exempt public charities under Internal Revenue Code section 501(c)(3) and corresponding statutes and that have a demonstrated interest in nurturing Christian faith and life were eligible to apply. ... The submission window for this initiative is now closed. ... Interested charitable organizations were able to submit proposals by May 18, 2026.

grant: Nurturing Children Through Worship and Prayer Initiative (incl. Initiative II)
eligibility: Interested charitable organizations with Internal Revenue Code section 501(c)(3) and public charity status that are committed to supporting Christian congregations are eligible to participate in Nurturing Children. Eligible organizations may submit proposals of up to $1.25 million each that may be used for up to a five-year period(2024 round, now closed).

grant: Serving Neighbors Through Congregational Collaborations Initiative
eligibility: Charitable organizations with Internal Revenue Code section 501(c)(3) and public charity status that are interested in and committed to supporting Christian congregations and local charitable organizations ... may include, among others: national and regional denominational agencies, faith-based service organizations, church associations and networks ... Individual congregations and local charitable organizations seeking resources for their own programs and services are not eligible to apply.

grant: Capital Grants for Historic Houses of Worship
eligibility: The National Fund for Sacred Places provides matching grants of $50,000 to $500,000 to congregations undertaking significant capital projects at historic houses of worship, along with wraparound services including training, technical assistance, and planning support.

grant: Making Parishes Everyone's Home (Parish Mentorship Initiative)
eligibility: The Making Parishes Everyone's Home program trains teams of parish and diocesan leaders in disability-ministry best practices: 'an opportunity for teams of parish and diocesan leaders from different areas of the country to work together for two years to advance disability support in their respective locations,' backed by a $500,000 Lilly Endowment grant (Thriving Congregations Initiative, December 2023). Participant training, peer mentorpairing, and funded conference attendance — not cash grants to applicants. NCPD states plainly on its schools page: 'NCPD does not offer grants to Catholic Schools or persons seeking financial assistance to enhance or access disability-related initiatives and services.'

CorWorks is a parish transformation initiative from the OSV Institute for Catholic Innovation: teams of 3 to 4 people representing parish leadership apply with 'Active pastor support: supporting the cause, approving the direction, and 15 minutes a week to check in with your team.' Dioceses participate as endorsing partners, not administrators: 'Your diocese doesn't manage, facilitate, or fund CorWorks. OSV does — entirely.' Accepted parishes submit a $2,500 refundable deposit at acceptance (returned on completion of the 3-month implementation roadmap); hardship accommodations available; no program fee.

grant: Domestic Grant Program (Spring and Fall cycles)
eligibility: US applicants: 501(c)(3) public charity, Catholic and listed in the Official Catholic Directory/P.J. Kenedy & Sons (edition and page number required on the form). Requests by and for individuals NOT accepted; no endowments, debt reduction, or influencing legislation. Construction/renovation over $200,000 requires 50% of cost in hand, signed contract, and work underway. Domestic applications require a Letter from the Ordinary (Bishop/Archbishop/Cardinal/Provincial) acknowledging the project, on official letterhead.

grant: Beyond Sunday Scholarships (tuition assistance and school grants)
grantor: Roman Catholic Foundation of Eastern Missouri
eligibility: Beyond Sunday Elementary Scholarships and Beyond Sunday Fellows (High School): tuition assistance 'for middle-income families seeking Catholic education for their children,' with preference for Catholic families registered in a parish of the Archdiocese of St. Louis; '26-'27 guidelines posted. The site's only other grant content is 'Grant Resources: General — Past Grant Recipients (2020 | 2019 | 2018 | 2017)' — no open general grant cycle is listed. The St. Martha Giving Circle pools member gifts and votes annually on beneficiaries that must be 'parishes, schools and ministries and other non-profit organizations located within the Archdiocese of St. Louis.'

To qualify to apply for a grant from Scanlan Foundation, your organization must be a Roman Catholic, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization in the State of Texas. Scanlan Foundation does not make grants to individuals. Each organization may only submit one unsolicited application per calendar year; (arch)dioceses may submit two. Dioceses and archdioceses should use the Diocese Grant Application Form unless the request is on behalf of an individual campus ministry or an independent ministry with its own tax-exempt letter. Applications by email as PDF forms to grants@scanlanfoundation.org; late applications not accepted.

The Serra International Foundation funds only programs that foster and promote vocations to the ministerial priesthood and religious life in the Catholic Church. Funding Priorities: Priestly and Religious Formation; Vocations Outreach; Spiritual Formation of Clergy and Religious. The grant application is open year-round with a September 30 deadline to apply for the next year's funding cycle, and the competitive grant cycle is open to organizations worldwide.

grant: Society for the Propagation of the Faith (mission grants/subsidies)
grantor: Society for the Propagation of the Faith (The Pontifical Mission Societies USA)
eligibility: Support flows to 'the proclamation of the Gospel, the building of the Church, and the work and witness of mission priests, religious Sisters and Brothers, and lay pastoral leaders' in the Pope's missions — i.e., mission territories abroad. Testimony from recipients (e.g., Archbishop of Dhaka, Bangladesh) describes annual ordinary subsidies that 'keep parishes running' in mission dioceses that 'cannot financially sustain it.'

A special, one-time matching grant opportunity available in 2026... designed to encourage chapters to create and lead new fundraising events that support new organizations or groups and engage new participants. Your event must be pre-approved, support a new 501(c)(3) cause aligned with Trusted Fraternal Life values, be a new event for your group, involve or invite new people, and be organized solely by your group. These grants are for Chapters, Lodges, Councils and Volunteer Teams.

grant: Catholic Campaign for Human Development (CCHD) Community & Economic Development Grants
grantor: USCCB Catholic Campaign for Human Development
eligibility: CCHD is 'the domestic anti-poverty program' of the USCCB; grants fund community development and economic development projects that 'address poverty's root causes' and empower low-income people, families, and communities (housing, healthy food, environmental justice, jobs, low-income leadership). Applications go through a Grant Eligibility and Inquiry Form and are screened, awarded, and monitored 'in close partnership with local Catholic dioceses'; the local bishop must review and endorse organizations working in the diocese.

grantor: USCCB Committee on Communications (Catholic Communication Campaign)
eligibility: Grants for communications projects that 'use media to spread the Gospel message and advance the USCCB's general mission goals.' Domestic projects must 'have the potential to reach a national audience' — the national CCC will NOT consider projects 'of an arch/diocesan or more local scope within the United States,' though projects 'that have a realistic potential for wider regional impact or for a particular population within the United States, may apply.' One request per organization per calendar year. Local-scope projects should seek the half of the diocesan CCC collection retained by the diocese.

grantor: USCCB Subcommittee on Catholic Home Missions
eligibility: Applications accepted from diocesan bishops of home mission dioceses (Class I), heads of interdiocesan/regional/national Catholic organizations, and provincials of religious institutes; 'AT THIS TIME, the Subcommittee is only approving grants to Class I applicants.' Every application needs the diocesan bishop's signature and endorsement plus audited financial statements.

grant: Legacy of Faith Faith Formation Grants
contact_name: Department of Evangelization, Education, and Youth Ministry
eligibility: Legacy of Faith: Parishes, missions, and ministries of the Diocese of Marquette are eligible for grants to help fund evangelization and faith formation programs and materials. Grant application is due April 1st of each year to fund programs taking place from July 1st through the following June.
